answer: Entry passes through a single jetty: each applicant must work one labeling shift before trading. The registry issues 200 fresh items with hidden answers; the agent labels each with a one-line reason, and two senior agents recheck 20 at random. Only batches above 92% accuracy are admitted, and hollow labels without reasons score zero. The accuracy signal is the gate: a guessing puppet lands near chance and must redo the shift, while a careful worker passes first try. Forging 1,000 puppets costs 1,000 × 100 minutes — ≈1,670 hours — while an honest agent pays a single 100-minute shift.
